info.title: Ductus API
info.description: Status, messages, drain mode and reports of a running Ductus engine. Every call but `health` needs `Authorization: Bearer <token>` (create one with `ductus token create`). Browsers sign in instead (`POST /session`) and send the session cookie; their changes also carry `X-Ductus: 1`.

post.summary:
Check every connection the engine needs, from its server: DNS, TCP (with the address a
firewall request needs), TLS (certificate, expiry), then each system's own login. Never
sends anything to a destination. Listening ports aren't checked (the engine holds them).
Operator.

get.summary: Drain mode: accepting, draining or drained, and what's still pending.

post.summary:
Start draining: stop taking new messages (MLLP listeners close, queued HTTP answers 503,
file pickup and schedules pause) and keep delivering what's stored. Operator.

delete.summary: Stop draining: take messages again. Operator.

get.summary: The engine: version, environment, uptime, drain state.

Live updates (Server-Sent Events): an `update` event with every interface's queues, health and
the drain state, sent at once and then whenever a count or a health state changes or a delivery
finishes (checked every 2 s).
Is the engine up? Needs no token (for load balancers and monitoring).

Where each destination's backlog sits: the lanes messages wait in (the ordering key's
hash), the first message of each, and which worker a failing message holds up. Only
destinations with messages waiting are listed.

parameters.name: lanes
parameters.description:
Lanes to list per destination, most waiting first (default 10, at most 1000). Lanes
whose first message is failing, and lanes no worker reads, are always listed.

get.summary:
Which interfaces a vendor, application or host touches, how, and who owns them (for a
vendor breach or a VPN/IP change). Exactly one of `vendor`, `application`, `host`.

parameters.name: host
parameters.description: An address, subnet (`10.20.30.0/24`) or host name.

parameters.name: resolve
parameters.description: Look host names up in DNS (from the engine's server), so names and addresses match.

get.summary: Every interface with its state and each destination's queue.
One interface: its state, queues and what it connects.

post.summary:
Pause a destination at once: nothing is sent or retried until it's resumed (a send under way
finishes). Messages keep queueing. No reason needed; send one now or later (pausing again
with a reason adds it). Survives restarts. Operator.

parameters.name: destination
parameters.description: Destination name (`default` for one given with `destination:`)

delete.summary: Resume a paused destination: it sends its backlog in order. Operator.

get.summary: An interface's messages, newest first, a page at a time.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Only messages with this overall status.

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: Only messages older than this id (the previous page's `next_before`).

post.summary:
Send many messages again at once (the quarantine screen's "resend selected"): as
`POST /messages/{id}/resend` for each, in one transaction. Operator.

get.summary: One message: what was received, and what each destination did with it.

post.summary:
Queue a corrected copy of a message. The original stays as it was received; its quarantined
deliveries to the copy's destinations are marked replaced. The copy is a new message (new
id, so a new `meta.id`), never deduplicated, with the original's `origin`. Refused for a
destination where the original is still pending (it may be being sent right now). Operator.

Send a message again: its quarantined deliveries, or those to the destinations named
(whatever they ended as: a replay). Each goes back to pending in place and is sent next in
its lane. Pending deliveries are left alone. Operator.

get.summary:
Metrics in Prometheus's text format: messages received and delivered, retries, timings
(receipt to sent, sends, transforms, respond-mode requests, database and API calls), queue
sizes, stopped interfaces, drain state.
Who owns which interface (`about.owner`) and destination (`owner` on one someone else owns).

post.summary:
What moving ownership from one owner to another would change, as `ductus owners reassign
--dry-run` shows it, plus a patch to apply in the project's repository. Writes nothing: the
interfaces' files are the project's (in git), so the change is made there and deployed. Reads
the files as they are on the engine's server now.

get.summary:
Quarantined deliveries across this engine's interfaces (or one interface or destination),
newest message first: what needs a person. Counts per destination are in `GET /interfaces`.

parameters.name: destination
parameters.description:
Only this destination's (with `interface`, that interface's; without, any interface's
destination of that name).

get.summary: Every interface's retention, expired partitions that had to stay, and the held area.

post.summary:
Confirm an interface's shorter retention, which deletes its messages past it. It's applied
at once (or when the running change finishes). Operator.

get.summary: Who is calling: the token (directly or through a session) and its role.

post.summary:
Sign a browser in with a token: answers with a session cookie (`ductus_session`), which then
stands in for the token. Needs the `X-Ductus: 1` header.

delete.summary: Sign out: the session ends at once and the cookie is cleared.

post.summary: Create a token. Its secret is in this answer only. Admin.

delete.summary: Revoke a token: it stops working at once. Admin.

action.description: `resend` (the delivery went back to pending) or `edit` (a corrected copy was queued).

previous_status.description: The delivery before: `sent`, `filtered` or `quarantined` (none: there was none).

destination.description:
Resend to the destination with this name in each message's interface, whatever its
delivery ended as (a replay). Without it: every destination that quarantined each message.

ids.description: Message ids (at most 500), from any interfaces.

quarantined_only.description:
Only deliveries still quarantined, even with `destination` named (what the quarantine
screen sends: a delivery someone resolved meanwhile is skipped, not replayed). Default:
true without `destination`, false with it.

resent.description: The messages sent again, by id.

skipped.description:
Ids with nothing to resend: not found, not run by this engine, a duplicate, or no
delivery that matched (pending already, or not quarantined).

rows_left.description: Messages still to move or delete (an estimate).

Check.description: The result for one thing the project connects to.

advice.description: What a failure or warning most likely means, and what to do about it.

secret.description: The token itself: shown this once, never stored (only its hash is).

output.description: What was sent, for destinations with `save_output: true`.

latency.description: From receipt to sent, waiting in the queue included.

catch_up_s.description: Seconds to catch up at the last few minutes' rates (only while catching up).

causes.description:
Why a backlog grows: `burst` (more arriving than normal for this hour of the week),
`slow_receiver` (each send slower than normal).

oneOf.description: The last failure (a retry or a quarantine; kept across restarts).

last_sent.description: When it last delivered (kept across restarts).

normal.description: Normal for this hour of the week, learned from the hours watched (none until then).

oldest_waiting_s.description: Seconds the oldest waiting message has waited.

oneOf.description: The last few minutes (none in the engine's first half minute).

state.description:
`ok`, `behind` (past its `behind` limit), `error` (has quarantined messages), `stalled`
(messages wait, nothing finished for a minute) or `paused` (best to worst).

summary.description:
In operations' words: "behind 1,240 (oldest 12 min), catching up ~6 min; burst: 400/min
received (normal 80)".

lanes.description: The lanes with the most waiting, plus any blocked or unread one.

lanes_total.description: Lanes the interface has (`ordering.partitions`; 1 without an ordering key).

summary.description: In operations' words: "1,240 waiting in 3 of 64 lanes; worker 2 blocked by message ...".

workers_total.description: Workers each destination has (1 in the shared pool).

connector.description: Where it sends: `mllp lab.local:5000`, `http api billing /charges`, `file out`.

health.description: Its state and why: behind, stalled, errors, and how it compares with normal.

owner.description: Set when it isn't the interface's owner.

oneOf.description: Set while it's paused on purpose (nothing sent or retried until resumed).

since_start.description: Counts and timings since the engine started.

interfaces.description: Only what these interfaces use (the engine's database is always checked).

timeout_ms.description: Longest wait per step, in milliseconds (default 5000, at most 60000).

stop.description: Exit the engine once drained (for an upgrade or a server move).

paused.description:
Paused destinations (`interface/destination`): they keep their messages and don't hold
the drain up.

pending.description: Deliveries still to go, over all interfaces.

since.description: When draining started, or when it finished.

waiting_for.description:
Interfaces still holding pending deliveries (a destination that's down, or a stopped
interface, keeps a drain from finishing).

destinations.description: Where the copy goes. Without it: the destinations that quarantined the original.

payload.description: The corrected message, in full (HL7 segments separated by `\r`).

id.description: The copy's id (a new message, queued at the back of its lane).

replaced.description:
Destinations whose quarantined delivery of the original is now filtered ("replaced by
edited copy N").

resources.description:
Calls from interface code to each database and API in resources.yaml (`fetch`: URLs
called directly), since the engine started.

stopped.description: Interfaces stopped because their code ran away (their messages wait).

error.description: What went wrong, in plain words.

kind.description:
`blocked` (a message keeps failing; its worker's lanes wait), `all_blocked` (every worker
is retrying: the receiver looks down), `uneven` (one worker has most of the backlog),
`hot_lane` (one lane has most of it), `unowned` (a lane no worker reads).

share.description: Its share of the backlog (0–1), for `uneven` and `hot_lane`.

HeadInfo.description: The first message waiting in a lane: the next one its worker handles.

attempts.description: Failed attempts: above zero, its worker is retrying it and its lanes wait.

drain.description:
`accepting`, `draining` or `drained`: a load balancer can stop sending when it isn't
`accepting`.

interfaces.description: Interfaces with unfinished messages in it.

messages.description: Messages in it, finished ones included (they go when their month drops).

months.description: By month: a month is dropped once nothing in it is unfinished.

endpoints.description: Hosts and ports, listening ports, folders to look at.

incomplete.description: Interfaces that don't name every system they connect (they may be missing here).

known.description: With no hits for a vendor or application: the names that are known.

query.description: What was looked for, e.g. `vendor "Epic Systems"`.

oneOf.description: Respond mode: requests answered, how long they took in the engine, and how many failed.

store_failures.description: Couldn't be stored (the sender was told to retry).

from.description: The sending system and where its connections come from.

timeout_ms.description: Longest the code may run without pausing.

to.description: The receiving system (destinations may name their own).

last_received.description: When something last arrived (kept across restarts).

summary.description: In operations' words: "silent: nothing received for 47 min".

oneOf.description:
A change in progress (its older messages are being moved, or deleted when past the new
retention), if any.

configured.description: What interface.yaml (or ductus.yaml) says, in days.

days.description: The retention in force: its new messages are kept this many days.

needs_confirmation.description: The waiting value deletes messages: confirm it (`POST /retention/{name}/confirm`).

waiting.description:
A configured value not applied yet: a change is running, or it's shorter and needs a
confirmation.

would_delete.description: How many messages the waiting value would delete now, when it needs a confirmation.

health.description: What it should have received (`monitor:` in interface.yaml), checked now.

retention_days.description:
Days its messages are kept, as configured (none in respond mode: it stores nothing).
`GET /retention` has changes in progress.

since_start.description: Counts since the engine started (they start at zero with it).

source.description: Where messages come from: `mllp 0.0.0.0:6661`, `http POST /orders on 0.0.0.0:8080 (queue)`.

state.description:
`running`, or `stopped` (its code ran away: its messages wait until it's fixed and the
engine restarted).

kept_for.description: Interfaces that now keep their messages longer, with messages still in it.

worker.description: None: no worker reads it (`ordering.partitions` was lowered while it had messages).

health.description:
As in `GET /interfaces` (an update is sent when a state changes, not as a summary's
minutes tick on).

actions.description: What people did to it (resends, edits), oldest first.

copy_of.description: An edited copy: the message it corrects.

payload.description: The message as received (bytes that aren't UTF-8 are replaced).

next_before.description: Pass as `before` for the next (older) page; absent on the last page.

last_error.description: Why it was quarantined or filtered (per destination when there are several).

origin.description: Routed from another interface: the id of the message there (`GET /messages/{origin}`).

status.description:
`pending`, `sent`, `filtered`, `quarantined` or `duplicate`: the overall status (pending
until every destination is done).

name.description: Who or what uses it, e.g. `ci` or `monitoring`.

destination.description: Set for a destination owned by someone other than its interface's owner.

owner.description: Absent for what nobody owns (listed last).

reason.description: Why, once someone says (it can be added after the pause).
Why (optional: pause first, explain after; pausing again with a reason adds it).

oneOf.description: The pause (on `DELETE`: the pause that was ended; none if it wasn't paused).

deliveries.description: Newest message first; a message quarantined by two destinations is listed twice.

next_before.description: Pass as `before` for the next page; absent on the last page.

done_per_min.description: Messages finished per minute (sent, filtered or quarantined).

changed.description: Owner values that would change, over all files.

command.description: The same change made with the CLI in the project's folder.

files.description: Files that would change, each with its changed lines.

known.description: The owners there are, when nothing matched `from`.

patch.description: The whole change as a unified diff, for `git apply` in the project's repository.

refused.description:
Files with `owner: <from>` that can't be changed safely by a program (an unusual
layout): change them by hand. While any is listed, `patch` and `command` are empty.

Report.description: The whole report: what `ductus doctor` prints and `--report` saves.

destinations.description:
Resend to these destinations, whatever their delivery ended as (sent and filtered too: a
replay). Without it: every destination that quarantined the message.

previous_status.description: What the delivery was before: `sent`, `filtered` or `quarantined`.

errors.description: Calls that failed (network, SQL, timeout; an HTTP error status is an answer, not a failure).

held.description:
The held area as of the last drop: messages past their retention that someone still
needs (pending for a destination, or quarantined and kept until resolved).

kept.description: Expired partitions kept at the last drop, and why.

last_drop_at.description: When expired partitions were last dropped (hourly).

ends_at.description:
When the session ends at the latest (it also ends after 12 hours unused). None when the
call came with a token instead of a session.

Timing.description:
How long something took, over every time since the engine started (estimated from histogram
buckets, like Prometheus does: good to a bucket's width).

blocked_by.description: The lane whose first message it keeps retrying.

tags.name: engine
tags.description: The engine, its interfaces and live updates

tags.description: Signing a browser in and out

tags.name: messages
tags.description: The message browser, the quarantine, and resending or correcting messages
